title: Ezekiel 40
paragraphs: ¹ In the twenty-fifth year of our exile, at the beginning of the year, on the tenth day of the month — in the fourteenth year after the city fell — on that very day the hand of the LORD was upon me and he brought me there. ² In visions of God he brought me to the land of Israel and set me on a very high mountain, on whose south side there was a structure that looked like a city. ³ He brought me there, and I saw a man whose appearance was like bronze. He stood at the gate, holding a linen cord and a measuring rod in his hand. ⁴ The man said to me, "Son of man, look carefully and listen closely, and pay attention to everything I am going to show you, for that is why you have been brought here. Report everything you see to the house of Israel." ⁵ I saw a wall completely surrounding the outside of the temple. The measuring rod in the man's hand was six long cubits, each cubit being a cubit and a handwidth. He measured the thickness of the wall — one rod — and its height — one rod.

⁶ Then he went to the gate that faces east. He climbed its steps and measured the threshold of the gate — one rod wide — and the other threshold — also one rod wide. ⁷ Each alcove was one rod long and one rod wide, with a space of five cubits between the alcoves. The gate threshold near the gate's inner porch was one rod deep. ⁸ He also measured the inner porch of the gate — one rod. ⁹ Then he measured the porch of the gate — eight cubits — and its jambs — two cubits. The gate porch faced inward. ¹⁰ On each side of the east gate were three alcoves. The three on each side were the same size, and the jambs on either side were the same size.

¹¹ He measured the width of the gate entrance — ten cubits — and the total length of the gateway — thirteen cubits. ¹² In front of each alcove was a ledge one cubit wide on each side. Each alcove was six cubits on one side and six cubits on the other. ¹³ He measured the gateway from the top of the rear wall of one alcove to the top of the opposite one — a width of twenty-five cubits from opening to opening. ¹⁴ He measured the jambs — sixty cubits tall — up to the courtyard all around the gate. ¹⁵ From the front of the entrance gateway to the front of the inner porch was fifty cubits.

¹⁶ The alcoves and their jambs had narrow windows all around the inside of the gateway, and the porticos also had windows all around the inside. Palm trees decorated the jambs. ¹⁷ Then he brought me into the outer court. I saw rooms and a pavement that had been made all around the court. Thirty rooms faced onto the pavement. ¹⁸ The pavement on both sides of the gates was as wide as the gates were long — this was the lower pavement. ¹⁹ Then he measured the distance from the front of the lower gateway to the front of the inner court — a hundred cubits on the east side and on the north side. ²⁰ The gate of the outer court that faced north — he measured its length and width.

²¹ It had three alcoves on each side, with jambs and porticos of the same measurements as the first gate — fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide. ²² Its windows, porticos, and palm trees were the same dimensions as those of the east gate. You went up seven steps to reach it, and its portico faced you as you approached. ²³ There was a gate to the inner court facing the north gate, just as there was one facing the east gate. He measured the distance from gate to gate — a hundred cubits. ²⁴ Then he led me to the south side, where I saw a gate facing south. He measured its jambs and porticos — they had the same dimensions as the others. ²⁵ The gate and its porticos had windows all around, like the previous windows — fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.

²⁶ Seven steps led up to it, and its portico faced the approach, with a palm tree on each side of the jambs. ²⁷ The inner court also had a gate facing south. He measured from that gate to the outer south gate — a hundred cubits. ²⁸ Then he brought me into the inner court through the south gate and measured it — it had the same measurements as the others. ²⁹ Its alcoves, jambs, and porticos all had the same dimensions, with windows all around. It was fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide. ³⁰ The porticos all around were twenty-five cubits long and five cubits wide.

³¹ Its porticos faced the outer court, and palm trees adorned the jambs. Eight steps led up to it. ³² He brought me to the inner court on the east side and measured the gate — it had the same dimensions as the others. ³³ Its alcoves, jambs, and porticos had the same measurements, and it had windows all around. It was fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide. ³⁴ Its porticos faced the outer court, with palm trees on both sides of the jambs. Eight steps led up to it. ³⁵ He brought me to the north gate and measured it — it had the same dimensions as the others.

³⁶ Its alcoves, jambs, and porticos were all there, with windows all around. The gate was fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide. ³⁷ Its jambs faced the outer court, and palm trees were on both sides of them. Eight steps led up to it. ³⁸ A room with a doorway opened onto the gateway porticos, where the burnt offerings were washed. ³⁹ Inside the gateway portico there were two tables on each side, where the burnt offerings, sin offerings, and guilt offerings were slaughtered. ⁴⁰ By the outer wall near the north gateway steps were two tables, and on the other side of the porch were two more tables.

⁴¹ So there were four tables inside the gateway and four outside — eight tables in all, on which the sacrifices were slaughtered. ⁴² There were also four tables of dressed stone for the burnt offerings, each one and a half cubits long, one and a half cubits wide, and one cubit high. The instruments used to slaughter the burnt offerings and other sacrifices were laid on these. ⁴³ Double hooks, each a handbreadth long, were fastened all around the inside walls, and the flesh of the offerings lay on the tables. ⁴⁴ Outside the inner gate, within the inner court, there were two rooms — one beside the north gate facing south, and one beside the east gate facing north. ⁴⁵ He said to me, "The room facing south is for the priests who have charge of the temple.

⁴⁶ The room facing north is for the priests who have charge of the altar. These are the sons of Zadok, who are the Levites who may approach the LORD to minister before him." ⁴⁷ He measured the inner court — a hundred cubits long and a hundred cubits wide, a perfect square. The altar stood in front of the temple. ⁴⁸ He brought me to the portico of the temple and measured the jambs of the portico — five cubits on each side. The gateway was fourteen cubits wide, with shoulders of three cubits on each side. ⁴⁹ The portico was twenty cubits wide and twelve cubits deep, with ten steps leading up to it, and pillars beside the jambs on both sides.
